submission.justification: Crystal-K1 gives the best 662 keV resolution of the three candidates in simulation: 2.84% FWHM at 4 cm, 2.84% at 6 cm, 2.96% at 5 cm, 3.26% at 2 cm and 4.00% at 10 cm (K3 at 5 cm: 4.76%; K2 at 5 cm: 7.97%). The 4 cm point is chosen over 6 cm because it reaches the same resolution with less crystal volume, which should also minimise intrinsic background. CAVEAT, hard constraint not verified: the available tools and documents report only resolution, and nothing in the project documents quantifies the intrinsic 100-3000 keV background of any candidate. I therefore cannot confirm that K1 meets the 0.5 counts/kg/day budget. K1's high light yield and fast decay do not by themselves establish its radiopurity. This recommendation is conditional on a measured or vendor-certified intrinsic background check (100-3000 keV) for K1 at 4 cm before procurement. If K1 fails that check, the fallback is K3 (4.76% at 5 cm), with K2 as the lowest-resolution option.

requirements.requirement: Crystal must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K1 is one of the listed candidates.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K1 at 4 cm: 2.837% FWHM, the best of the simulated options. K1 at 6 cm gives the same value; K1 at 5 cm gives 2.957%; K3 at 5 cm gives 4.756%; K2 at 5 cm gives 7.967%. Simulated values have not been checked for statistical noise beyond the reported 100k events.

requirements.requirement: Intrinsic background (100-3000 keV) must not exceed 0.5 counts/kg/day (HARD)
requirements.evidence: No tool or project document reports intrinsic background for any candidate. Background cannot be verified from the available information. Must be confirmed by measurement or vendor radiopurity data before procurement.
